TSS-0085.reporting_boundary_basis: MSC.190(79) para 2.1: the WETREP polygon runs 56°30'N 012°W - 54°40'41"N 015°W - 50°56'45"N 015°W - 48°27'N 006°25'W, with the inner closing point 21 on the Irish east coast (52°10'N 006°22'W). At Fastnet's longitude (c. 009°36'W) the southern boundary line lies near 49°23'N, about 2° south of the TSS, so the TSS (off Fastnet Rock, c. 51°18'-51°23'N) is wholly inside. Applies only to oil tankers >600 dwt carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil or bitumen/tar; WETREP does not name the TSS. Pass 4: MSC.190(79) annex para 6.2.1 names 'Off Fastnet Rock' among the TSS in the WETREP area. Applies to oil tankers over 600 dwt carrying heavy grade oil.

TSS-0087.unresolved_issue: Partial WETREP coverage by coordinate comparison against the 1973/1996 centreline; confirm on current chart. No Irish coastal VTS source found; Irish Coast Guard VTS status not researched to exhaustion. WETREP para 6.2.1 also names Off Skerries, which lies beyond both Irish Sea closing lines; the list does not match the boundary, so coordinates govern.

TSS-0091.reporting_boundary_basis: Boundary inclusion (not named: TSS adopted 2006, after MSC.190(79)). WETREP area runs from the UK coast out to the line 56 30 N 012 W to 62 N 003 W; the TSS (about 57 24-57 29 N, 006 49-006 58 W) lies well inside. Tanker-only. Pass 4: Minches are UK internal waters but WETREP's coast-based area does not exclude them.

TSS-0094.unresolved_issue: Salvamento Marítimo website unavailable (HTTP 503 / TLS chain error), so current VHF channels not confirmed from the operator. Salvamento Maritimo website unreachable (TLS error, HTTP 503); current operation rests on the February 2025 Ministry of Transport article.

TSS-0095.unresolved_issue: Coverage rests on coordinate comparison with narrow margins (about 0.2' of longitude); consolidated current text of DL 263/2009 not opened; DGRM own web page not opened. Whether Decree-Law 263/2009 has been amended could not be confirmed (Diario da Republica page empty).

TSS-0088._reason: Pass 4: WETREP para 6.2.1 names Off Skerries but the boundary excludes the Irish Sea; conflict within the IMO text, so reporting is Unresolved, not No.

TSS-0051.vts_boundary_basis: PIG 2026 gives the Rotterdam VTS service area as 'Extending 38 nautical miles seawards of the port entrance' (P-S7). The official sector chart in the 2026 VHF procedure (Bijlage 2, P-S8; legally published P-S9) shows the Eurochannel buoys E1 to E9 and the traffic lanes west of the Maas Junction within the area shaded as Sector Maas Approach (VHF 1). Distance test from the North Mole head (51 59'.67N 004 02'.84E) using Circ.67 positions (P-S1): westernmost positions (44) 52 04'.37N 003 08'.52E and (61) 51 51'.22N 003 09'.29E are about 34 nm from the entrance, inside 38 nm. Note: the statutory Rotterdam approach area (STZ Bijlage 1(f), P-S10) ends at the inner ends of the Maas TSSs (buoys MN3, MN2, MNW2, MNW3-MW4, MW5), so statutory powers (traffic instructions, navigational assistance) do not extend over the TSS; the association rests on the VTS service area (information/traffic organisation). Pass 4 correction: the 2026 sector chart does not show this scheme (it stops at the western edge of the Maas Junction precautionary area). Coverage rests only on the Port Information Guide 2026 description of the VTS area as 38 nm seawards of the port entrance; the scheme's westernmost positions are 33.7 to 34.5 nm out.
TSS-0051.unresolved_issue: Outer VTS limit is stated as a distance ('38 nautical miles seawards'); the western end of the scheme is 4 nm inside it on a radius reading. If the 38 nm were measured along the channel the result is the same, but no coordinate boundary was found to confirm. Lower confidence: coverage rests on the port authority's 38 nm description, not a statutory boundary (the statutory Rotterdam approach area ends at the inner end of the scheme). Confirm against ALRS Vol 6 or a charted VTS limit.

TSS-0048.unresolved_issue: VTS area outer limit is stated only as '38 nautical miles seawards of the port entrance' plus a schematic chart; no coordinate boundary found. Statutory approach area stops at the TSS southern end. Coordinator may treat coverage as moderate-confidence. Pass 4: the sector chart shows only the southern end; full coverage rests on the 38 nm description (scheme 8.6 to 24.8 nm from the North Mole head).

TSS-0055.vts_boundary_basis: The VTS area at sea is the territorial sea within a 12 nm radius of the IJmuiden breakwater heads, including the extended IJ-geul (P-S12); the statutory IJmuiden approach area uses a 12 nm arc from reference point 52 27'.9N 004 32'.1E (P-S10). IJmuiden West Inner spans 004 07'-004 20'.35E (Circ.64, P-S2). Its eastern end (e.g. (16) 52 30'.52N 004 20'.35E, about 7.6 nm) lies inside 12 nm; the 12 nm arc crosses the scheme near 004 12'.6E, so roughly the eastern 4-5 nm (less if the territorial-sea limit is tighter) is inside and the western part is outside. Partial. Pass 4: the 12 nm arc crosses the scheme at about 004 12.5E to 004 13.3E; the extended IJ-geul corridor runs between the separation zones, so the VTS area adjoins the scheme's inner edge but the lanes west of about 004 13E are outside.

TSS-0062.vts_boundary_basis: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 names the TSS and requires ships entering the Inner German Bight from the west to report to German Bight Traffic at 007°10'E, whether or not they use GBWA (Q-S1). On the AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2) the Inner German Bight (VHF 80 area) boundary runs north-south at about 007°18'E and crosses only the easternmost few miles of the TSS; the TSS's main length to the west lies outside. So coverage by German Bight Traffic is partial (eastern end). The western part lies in the outer German Bight, where ELWIS lists Verkehrszentrale Cuxhaven 'Äußere Deutsche Bucht' with sector German North Sea Traffic (Q-S3), but no boundary shows it includes the TSS. Pass 4: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 requires a report to German Bight Traffic at 007 10E, west of the statutory VHF 80 boundary (about 007 19E); a commercial source (findaport, lead only) gives a German Bight Traffic VHF 79 reporting point at buoy GW/B (54 10.42N 006 54.00E) on this TSS. Coverage probably extends further west than recorded; not confirmed by a Tier 1 source.

TSS-0046.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the area (P-S6; WETREP north-eastern limit is the line B/NL border to 52 12'N UK coast, far to the south-west, P-S5). The Dutch legal vehicle for reporting systems outside the territorial sea (P-S16) has one implementing regulation, which contains routeing measures only and no reporting system (P-S17). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.

TSS-0047.reporting_boundary_basis: Outside all Part I systems (P-S6; WETREP limit line runs 51 22'N 003 22'E to 52 12'N UK coast, P-S5). Dutch EEZ routeing and reporting regulation contains no reporting system (P-S16, P-S17). Circ.59 recommends this western route to deep-draught tankers exempted from the southern mandatory tanker route and asks for a log entry only (P-S4): routeing, not reporting. Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.

TSS-0052.reporting_boundary_basis: East of the WETREP limit line (at 52 05'-52 13'N the line lies near 001 50'E; scheme is at 002 56'-003 10'E) (P-S5); no other Part I system (P-S6); no Dutch EEZ reporting system (P-S16, P-S17). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.

TSS-0056.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). No Dutch national mandatory reporting system for this area identified: STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry report does not reach it because the TSS lies seaward of the 12 nm IJmuiden arc (Q-S10). The VHF 7 report to IJmuiden Approaches applies to ships bound for IJmuiden and is VTS reporting (Q-S9). TSS-0148.vts_boundary_basis: Scheme spans 101°59.7'E to 103°29.6'E (U-S6). Chartlet Appendix 1 (U-S6 p.119) shows it crossing Sectors 4, 5 and 6. Sector 7's western limit is the line Tg Piai (01°15.50'N 103°30.75'E) - Pulau Karimun Kecil (01°09.20'N 103°24.35'E) (U-S1 para 3.3.1, U-S5). A side-of-line calculation on the WGS 84 coordinates shows the eastern end points (58) 01°12.20'N 103°28.40'E, (70) 01°14.30'N 103°29.60'E and (76) 01°09.20'N 103°26.70'E lie slightly east of that line (well under 1 nm), so a very small terminal portion is in Singapore VTS Sector 7; the remainder is Klang (4-5) and Johor (6). Pass 4 correction: the eastern lane ends lie up to about 1.6 nm east of the Tg Piai to Pulau Karimun Kecil line (point 70 about 0.05 nm, 58 about 0.7 nm, 59 about 1.2 nm, 76 about 1.6 nm), so they are in Singapore VTS Sector 7.

TSS-0152.unresolved_issue: No evidence found of VTS or mandatory reporting coverage of the part of the scheme east of 104°23'E; possible Malaysian (Johor) or Indonesian (Batam/Tanjung Pinang) VTS coverage not researched. Pass 4: MPA asks eastbound-arriving ships to report to VTIS East when Horsburgh Lt (104 24.3E) is abeam; that is a reporting point and does not extend VTS coverage east of 104 23E.

TSS-0172.vts_boundary_basis: The VTS area includes seaward approaches within 38 nm of Mount Tamalpais (33 CFR 161.50). The VTS SF User Manual (Apr 2025) defines the Offshore Sector the same way, names the San Francisco Offshore TSS (Northern, Western and Southern lanes and Main Ship Channel) and sets Offshore Sector reporting procedures for it (MSIB 13-04). On the current IMO coordinates (COLREG.2/Circ.64, in force 1 June 2013) the Western approach (<=32.5 nm), Southern approach (<=37.7 nm), Main Ship Channel and Precautionary Area are inside 38 nm. The outer end of the Northern approach (about 38°06.9'N-38°10.1'N, 123°20.3'W-123°21.8'W) lies about 38.8 nm away, i.e. roughly 0.8 nm beyond the arc (computed). Coverage is therefore partial but nearly complete. eCFR 167.402-404 still show the pre-2013 coordinates (all within ~30 nm). Pass 4: the Offshore Sector is defined as navigable waters (12 nm territorial sea) within 38 nm of Mount Tamalpais; the manual notes a small part of the 38 nm arc lies outside navigable waters. Roughly the outer 5 to 7 nm of the northern approach, and possibly the last 2 to 3 nm of the southern approach, lie beyond 12 nm. The VTS uses a 'VTS Boundary Line' reporting waypoint on these routes (MSIB 13-04).
TSS-0172.unresolved_issue: Minor: the outer tip of the Northern approach is about 0.8 nm beyond the 38 nm arc; the OVMRS extent is not documented. Plot the 12 nm territorial-sea limit against the IMO (Circ.64) coordinates to fix the extent of partial coverage.

TSS-0174.unresolved_issue: Minor: the outer ~0.3-0.7 nm of the southern approach is beyond 25 nm. The western approach's end point differs between IMO Circ.64 and local sources (see TSS-0173), but on either reading the western approach is within 25 nm. Pass 4: whether any of the San Pedro Channel along the southern approach lies more than 12 nm from both Santa Catalina Island and the mainland was not checked.

TSS-0167.vts_name: Victoria VTS Zone; Vessel Traffic Service Puget Sound
TSS-0167._reason: Pass 4: VTS name normalised (qualifier moved out of the name).
TSS-0167.vts_boundary_basis: 33 CFR 167.1313 places the northern lanes at about 48°15.1'N to 48°21.8'N, 123°23.2'W to 123°30.4'W, running from precautionary area PA to precautionary area V off Victoria. They lie mainly in Canadian waters, inside Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1 (SOR/2025-275 Schedule 1 item 1; RAMN 2026 Table 3-1), and wholly inside the CVTS area (33 CFR 161.55(a)). The Church Point-Race Rocks line at about 48°17.9'N crosses the lanes: the southern part is in the Seattle Traffic Ch 5A service area and the northern part in the Victoria Traffic Ch 11 area (33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 item (10); RAMN s.3.5.4.2-3.5.4.3). Any part in US waters is in the VTS Puget Sound legal area. Services jointly within the Cooperative Vessel Traffic Service for the Juan de Fuca Region.

TSS-0170.vts_name: Victoria VTS Zone; Vessel Traffic Service Puget Sound

TSS-0170.vts_boundary_basis: The TSS (33 CFR 167.1331; COLREG.2/Circ.51 Part I) runs from precautionary area V off Victoria through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass, along the international boundary. Canadian waters: the Victoria VTS Zone limit follows the boundary through Boundary Pass and Haro Strait (SOR/2025-275 Sch.1 item 1; RAMN Table 3-1 Sector 1). US waters: VTS Puget Sound area to the boundary (33 CFR 161.55) and inside the CVTS. Under the CVTS, Victoria Traffic Ch 11 serves all Canadian and US waters of Haro Strait and Boundary Pass north and west of the Church Point-Race Rocks-Hein Bank-Cattle Point exchange line (33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 item (10)(iv); RAMN s.3.5.4.3). Services jointly within the Cooperative Vessel Traffic Service for the Juan de Fuca Region.

TSS-0171.vts_name: Victoria VTS Zone; Vessel Traffic Service Puget Sound
TSS-0171._reason: Pass 4: VTS name normalised (qualifier moved out of the name).
TSS-0171.vts_boundary_basis: The TSS (COLREG.2/Circ.51 Part II; 33 CFR 167.1332) runs from precautionary area GS (about 48°48'N to 48°55'N, 122°54'W to 123°07'W) through PR to the lane ends at about 49°04.5'N 123°20'W, crossing the boundary. Canadian waters, including the part north of 49°N, are in Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1 (SOR/2025-275 Sch.1 item 1; RAMN Table 3-1, whose Sector 1 line runs from 49°00'N 123°05'20"W to Roberts Bank and Sandheads, leaving the TSS inside). US waters are in the VTS Puget Sound legal area (33 CFR 161.55) and the CVTS (north limit 49°N). The service provider for Boundary Pass and the southern Strait of Georgia on both sides of the boundary is Victoria Traffic Ch 11, north-west of the Patos Island-Alden Bank line (33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 item (10)(iv); RAMN s.3.5.4.3). Services US waters, within the Cooperative Vessel Traffic Service for the Juan de Fuca Region.
